report.career_summary: Scott Knowles has three results in the archive spanning 2020 to 2026 — a marathon and two Waterfront Half Marathon starts. He is a recreational runner who has taken on serious distances, and his 1:34:52 half-marathon in 2025 is a meaningful personal best that represents genuine committed training. His 2020 Auckland Marathon (3:44:13) was completed at age 30 in a field of 1,619, finishing in the top 25% — a creditable debut for a first or early marathon. He has shown the consistency of someone who keeps coming back to racing across multiple years.
report.trajectory: With only three results across two distances, trend analysis is limited. The progression from a 3:44 marathon in 2020 to a 1:34:52 half-marathon PB in 2025 spans a five-year gap and different distances, making direct comparison difficult. The 2025 Waterfront Half PB suggests his fitness improved meaningfully between 2020 and 2025. His 2026 Waterfront result (2:29:05) is a significant outlier — nearly an hour slower than his 2025 PB at the same event — likely reflecting a very difficult race day, an injury, or a training run rather than a fitness regression. Taking the 2025 PB as the benchmark, his trajectory is one of steady progress.
report.best_result: Knowles's best field-relative result is his Waterfront Half Marathon 2025 finish — 309th from 2,200 finishers, placing him in the 86th percentile. Finishing in the top 15% of a 2,200-person half-marathon is a genuinely good result for a recreational runner, and reflects a sustained 1:34 pace across 21.1 km. His 2020 Auckland Marathon result (398th of 1,619, top 25%) is a comparable achievement in a much larger and more competitive field. Both results show a runner who finishes respectably in the broader participant population.
report.distance_profile: Knowles has raced both the marathon and half-marathon, with more recent activity at 21.1 km. His half PB (1:34:52) projects to a marathon equivalent of roughly 3:20–3:30 using standard conversion ratios, suggesting his 2020 marathon of 3:44 may have been slightly undertrained for the distance, or simply reflects how much he has improved since. A focused build targeting a 3:20–3:30 marathon finish would be realistic based on his current half-marathon fitness. The shorter distance appears to be his current focus and is the distance where he has the most recent and reliable data.
report.where_to_race: Waterfront Half Marathon in March is clearly Knowles's race — he has done it twice and set his PB there in 2025. The course starts and finishes in Auckland's CBD and is well-organised with strong community support, making it a good home event. For a marathon, Auckland Marathon in October is the natural progression — he has already completed it, knows the course, and the October timing gives a full year to train from a March half. Queenstown Marathon is worth considering for the experience if he wants a change of scenery, though the hillier course would likely return slower times.
report.qualifying_note: Knowles's current marathon PB (3:44:13) is outside the Boston qualifying standard for M 30–39 (3:00:00) by approximately 44 minutes. Reaching Boston qualifying territory would require a substantial step up in training volume and consistency — roughly a 44-minute improvement — which is achievable over 2–4 years with a structured programme but is a long-term goal rather than near-term. His half-marathon PB converts to a marathon estimate of approximately 3:20–3:30, so a sub-3:30 marathon is a realistic intermediate target before thinking about Boston.
